static_traits.name: Li Jingna
static_traits.family_status: Living alone, limited contact with extended family
static_traits.social_status: Tense relationships with friends, often seeking others' approval for stamp collecting; has a few close friends but has not yet discussed this issue with them
static_traits.medical_history: No major physical illness; no similar psychological problems before; no psychotherapy or counseling received
static_traits.language_features: Clear expression, coherent logic; rather negative attitude, often using comparative and negating statements; skeptical about change but willing to try, fair cooperation

basic_info.main_problem: I keep worrying that my stamp collection has no valuable stamps, which makes me believe the whole collection is worthless.
basic_info.core_demands: This sense of worthlessness is starting to affect my daily life and Work performance; I want to learn how to cope with it effectively.
growth_experiences: After talking with a stamp-collecting friend who owns many high-value stamps a few months ago, I began to realize my collection is not valuable, triggering moderate stress and a sense of worthlessness; since then, every time Looking at one's stamp collection and When comparing oneself with others, these feelings are triggered, gradually developing into being unable to enjoy the collection and affecting Work focus.

Once found a rare (but not very expensive) stamp at a flea market, feeling very excited and proud at the time, experiencing the value and joy of collecting; such moments have become relatively fewer, but they remain memories of positive experiences.

special_situations.event: A conversation with stamp-collecting friends, the other person owns several very valuable stamps
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If my collection is not as valuable as others', it means I am a failure and have no value
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Repeatedly reorganizes the collection and frequently seeks recognition from other collectors to prove their collection is valuable
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: My collection is not valuable, I am not as good as him

special_situations.event: Each time viewing one's own stamp collection and comparing with others' collections
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: A collection's value is either very high or utterly meaningless, with no middle ground
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Repeatedly picking at the collection's shortcomings, ignoring existing highlights and joys
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: Because I lack one very valuable stamp, my whole collection is worthless

special_situations.event: Thinking at work about the valuable stamps missing from their collection
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If the collection is not valuable enough, I cannot work with peace of mind, and Work performance will worsen
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: While at work, distracted by worries about the collection, unable to focus
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: I cannot focus, Work will get worse and worse

special_situations.event: Seeking approval from other collectors but not yet finding relief
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: Only if others recognize it does my collection count as valuable
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Continuously seeks external evaluation and affirmation
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: If they do not approve, my collection is really not valuable

core_conflict.wish: Longs to be recognized, seen, and affirmed (including the value of self and the collection)
core_conflict.fear: Fearing appearing worthless after comparison, being belittled and humiliated, thus losing self-esteem and relationships
defense_goal: Maintains self-worth by adhering to external standards and seeking others' recognition
Avoiding shame and judgment by distancing from friends

object_relations.self_representation: A not-good-enough comparer/collector of insufficient value
object_relations.object_representation: Picky, judgmental superior people (those with rarer collections)

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When the counselor suggests viewing the collection from a more balanced perspective and focusing on its positive aspects
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: Subconsciously understanding suggestions as denying reality, worrying one's shortcomings will be ignored yet still judged
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Using absolutist and value-standardizing wording (like 'no matter what, not good enough'), in a rather cold tone, reducing emotional vocabulary, emphasizing logic and rules.

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When seeing others own more valuable stamps or when talking about When comparing oneself with others
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: Turning the post-comparison Sense of frustration toward the self, believing one has no value overall
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Responding in a self-blaming, Self-deprecation tone (like 'I just cannot do it'), lowering self-evaluation, avoiding expressing dissatisfaction with others.

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When hearing or mentioning external standards and evaluations about collection value
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: Uncritically treating others' standards as the only correct criterion, believing one must own expensive rare stamps to be valuable
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Citing authority or others' views as basis, using 'should/must' statements, in a firm tone, maintaining an excluding attitude toward different views.

manifestations: Feeling 'everything is utterly meaningless' when looking at one's stamp collection
No longer able to enjoy the hobby, believing the collection as a whole is worthless
outcomes: Loss of interest and reduced pleasure

manifestations: Living alone, limited contact with extended family
Distant from friends due to embarrassment, rarely talks about one's troubles
outcomes: Negative emotions accumulate in private settings

contact_model.definition: The individual takes in external rules and expectations without digesting them, treating them as their own standards or absolute truths, corresponding to 'rejection'. Language manifestations include: 'I must/should...', 'Everyone is like this', and so on.
manifestations: Takes others' standards for a 'valuable collection' directly as his own sole standard
Using absolutist 'should/must' judgments when evaluating the collection (like 'without prestigious stamps it does not count as valuable')

contact_model.definition: The individual has a poor capacity for self-reflection and introspection, with excessive self-restriction and self-blame, and is overly cautious about contact, corresponding to 'autonomy'.
manifestations: Frequent Self-denial (like 'my collection is not good enough')
Distancing from friends out of worry about being compared and judged

contact_model.definition: The individual ignores or avoids a stimulus from the internal or external environment, deliberately avoiding direct contact, corresponding to 'acceptance'.
manifestations: When invited to focus on the positive (organization and historical interest), quickly returning to negative comparison and negation
Ignores moments in the collection that made oneself excited and proud

exception_events.target_problem: When Looking at one's stamp collection and When comparing oneself with others, the client usually develops a strong sense of worthlessness and cannot enjoy the collection, further affecting Work focus.
exception_events.unique_outcome: Once discovering a rare stamp at a flea market (though not very expensive), not falling into comparison at the moment but feeling excited and proud, experiencing the value and joy of collecting.
exception_events.reason: Different situation: obtaining concrete success clues in the chance encounter at the flea market; different approach: focusing on the joy of discovery and research rather than comparison; different understanding: viewing 'rarity' as the value of personal exploration rather than purely monetary value.

positive_force: Interested in organizing the collection and historical research, able to identify highlights
Able to recall and acknowledge positive moments (such as discoveries at the flea market)
Willing to try cognitive restructuring and homework, has willingness to change
Having a few dependable friend resources (though not yet discussed this issue)
negative_force: Mental filtering and negating the positive, over-focusing on shortcomings
Overly depends on external recognition and comparison to define self-worth
Shame and inferiority causing distance from friends, Reduced social support
Distracted at work worrying about the collection; hard to concentrate

target_behavior.behavior: Repeatedly compares one's stamp collecting with others and continuously seeks external recognition
antecedent: Talks with stamp-collecting friends or encounters other collectors' evaluations
target_behavior.core_reason: Strongly ties self-worth to the monetary rarity of the collection, and interprets the 'lack of prized stamps' catastrophically
target_behavior.function: Gaining external approval to temporarily relieve the sense of worthlessness; escaping inner unease and shame
target_behavior.consequence: Tense relationships with friends, unable to enjoy collecting, negative emotions intensified

target_behavior.behavior: Unfocused attention at Work, occupied by collection-related negative thinking
antecedent: Thinking at work about the valuable stamps missing from their collection
Browses or recalls others' high-value collections before and after work
target_behavior.core_reason: Emotional reasoning and catastrophizing: generalizes the disappointment with the collection to the work domain, believing he will perform poorly
target_behavior.function: Gaining a sense of 'control' through worry and self-criticism, while avoiding uncertainty at Work
target_behavior.consequence: Decline in work performance, impaired focus, further reinforcing Self-denial
